news.title: Local bodies in Tamil Nadu get expanded powers to approve building plans
news.para: The Tamil Nadu government has simplified the approval process for residential building plans by local bodies. Corporations and municipalities can now approve plans with greater floor space and more dwelling units. Town panchayats and rural bodies have also seen an increase in their approval limits. The height limit for residential and commercial buildings has been increased to enhance the availability of space.

news.title: ED raids 13 places across Delhi-NCR, Bengaluru, Chandigarh in fraudulent NRI housing loan case
news.para: The Enforcement Directorate conducted searches at 13 properties associated with a major money laundering case. Focused on fraudulent housing loans secured with forged documents for Non-Resident Indians, the investigation involves entities such as Antriksh Promoters and Developers Pvt Ltd and Sunshine Infrawell Pvt Ltd. The collection of evidence aims to uncover financial irregularities, potentially leading to the seizure of crucial documents and digital assets.

news.title: Uttar Pradesh housing board's NOC not needed for building plan approval
news.para: The housing department has announced that property owners will no longer require no-objection certificates from the UP Housing Board. This change abolishes outdated regulations from a 2010 directive, allowing direct submission of building plans to the Lucknow Development Authority. Additionally, betterment fees for housing board schemes will not be included with development authority project fees, streamlining the approval process to foster urban growth in the state.

news.title: LuLu International leases 62,035 sq ft retail space in Greater Noida for 15 years
news.para: LuLu International Shopping Malls has secured a significant 62,035 square foot lease at I-Thums Galleria, located in Greater Noida. This 15-year agreement with Adihm Developers initiates with a monthly rent of about ₹26.42 lakh, which will see increments every three years. Over its duration, the total rent is estimated at ₹56.9 crore, not including additional expenses. Both parties have established lock-in periods as part of the contract.

news.title: Noida: Wish Town residents protest against shared area maintenance fees
news.para: Residents of Jaypee Wish Town are voicing their discontent over the Suraksha Group's newly introduced shared area maintenance charge. Starting in November, residents will face an increase of Rs 1.5 per square foot, pushing their monthly fees from Rs 6,000 to an alarming Rs 10,000. They are questioning the fairness of covering additional costs for facilities used by others.

news.title: IBM India leases 2.83 lakh sq ft office space in Bengaluru for 10 years
news.para: IBM India has leased an extensive office space at Radon tower in Bagmane Solarium City. The lease agreement spans over a decade, with estimated costs totaling Rs 522 crore. IBM will pay a monthly base rent of Rs 2.49 crore, subject to a 15% escalation every three years. Additionally, the company will incur fit-out costs over five years, approximately amounting to Rs 179 crore.

news.title: India real estate deal value falls 76% while PE investment dips 35% in Q3 2026: Report
news.para: In the third quarter of 2026, India's real estate market faced significant challenges, with total deal values plummeting to $705 million, reflecting a staggering 76% drop compared to the previous year. Notably, private equity investments dwindled to $555 million across just nine transactions. The commercial sector remained the backbone, representing 57% of all deal value as investors shifted focus towards stability in cash flows amid the turmoil.

news.title: NHB appoints forensic auditor for SRG Housing Finance
news.para: The National Housing Bank (NHB) has appointed ASA & Associates LLP to conduct a forensic audit of SRG Housing Finance amid allegations of fictitious loan accounts worth ₹300–400 crore, repayment record manipulation and possible fund diversion. The investigation will examine loan disbursements, borrower identities, asset classifications and fund usage, with findings potentially shaping regulatory action and the lender’s financial outlook.

news.title: The LaLiT Suri Hospitality Group plans ₹600 crore expansion; to add about 1,000 keys
news.para: The LaLiT Suri Hospitality Group plans to invest ₹600 crore and add about 1,000 keys to its existing inventory of 2,300 keys, with roughly half of the new capacity coming through owned properties and the balance through management contracts.

news.title: Shree Cement’s net profit declines 15% to ₹263.46 crore in Q2 FY27
news.para: Shree Cement has seen a 15 percent drop in net profit for the second quarter of FY27, even as total income rose by 21.6 percent compared to last year. The company's domestic sales volume grew by 18 percent year-on-year, and its ready-mix concrete division significantly boosted sales volume and revenue. Despite facing obstacles, Shree Cement is aggressively pursuing new capacity expansions and initiatives for future growth.

news.title: Godrej Properties’ net profit declines 64% to ₹145.47 crore in Q2 FY27
news.para: In Q2 FY27, Godrej Properties faced a significant decline in net profit after tax, dropping 63.9 percent. Despite this setback, the company saw a total income increase of 31.9 percent, totaling ₹2,571.73 crore. The booking value for the quarter soared to ₹8,008 crore from the sale of 3,658 units, while collections rose by 31 percent to ₹5,318 crore, demonstrating positive operating cash flow with a jump to ₹1,584 crore.

news.title: CAQM issues notices to MCG, GMDA chiefs over dust-control failure in Gurugram
news.para: The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) has formally issued show-cause notices to officials from MCG and GMDA due to serious lapses in pollution control efforts. These notices highlight 258 separate instances of inadequate dust management on various roads throughout Gurgaon, compelling both agencies to explain their failure to comply with earlier directives. As public dissatisfaction regarding air quality surges, the efficacy of existing pollution-control initiatives is being intensely evaluated.

news.title: Dhanbad administration identifies 180 illegal houses on government land
news.para: A land survey in Dhanbad identified 180 houses and a marriage hall built illegally on government property. Residents expressed concern as many were relocated to Baramuri Khatal in 2005. Authorities plan to issue eviction notices to the occupants for unauthorized structures. Police also arrested a man for possessing illegal firearms in the area during a separate operation. Investigations are ongoing regarding other individuals involved in the illegal activities.

news.title: Property registrations in Mumbai  fall 4% on working-day basis during Navratri 2026
news.para: Mumbai recorded 4,680 property registrations during Navratri 2026, 25% lower than last year’s 6,238 registrations. However, the two periods had a different number of registration days; average registrations per working day declined 4% year-on-year to 669 units.

news.title: The future of Bavdhan's commercial heart: Flow Bavdhan
news.para: In 2022, Flow Bavdhan launched as a premium shopping hub, significantly elevating the retail and dining experiences in Bavdhan. This initiative fulfills the demand for organized retail, offering visitors a vibrant marketplace atmosphere. The design encourages community interaction and exploration, while its strategic positioning links it to major residential and professional areas in Pune. Tayal Corp is committed to delivering enduring value to the community through this development.

news.title: Wonder Cement & Dalmia Bharat's limestone mining projects near Rajasthan's Great Indian Bustard 'priority area' approved
news.para: Rajasthan's Jaisalmer region has given the green light to two limestone mining initiatives that encounter the habitats of the Great Indian Bustard. One project intrudes on a designated priority area, while the other lies a kilometer away. Despite concerns over the longevity of endangered species conservation, these projects were approved, with environmental assessments indicating minor impacts and the need for ongoing monitoring and protective measures.

news.title: Lucknow development body plans levy charge to fund pending works in Sushant Golf City
news.para: In Sushant Golf City, property owners may face a new completion charge tied to building approvals. This fee is intended to support ongoing infrastructure projects, covering crucial developments like roadways and sewage systems. However, plot holders of EWS and LIG with smaller plots will be exempt, benefitting more than 10,000 allottees. The Lucknow Development Authority aims to enhance the completion procedure to better manage the township's future.

news.title: Property fraud cases rise in South Goa despite SIT probe
news.para: South Goa is witnessing a surge in land-grab activities and property fraud. The police have taken action by registering several FIRs against these criminal acts. Notably, one complaint revolves around false claims of land ownership and suspicious contracts between involved parties. Additionally, there’s a case of property being improperly used as collateral for a hefty bank loan.

news.title: Uttar Pradesh: UPEIDA launches industrial plot scheme in eight clusters
news.para: The Uttar Pradesh Expressways Industrial Development Authority (UPEIDA) is rolling out a new initiative to distribute industrial plots within eight Integrated Manufacturing and Logistics Clusters located in cities such as Meerut and Hardoi. The land premiums vary between Rs 3,800 and Rs 11,470 per square metre, and interested businesses can apply online via the Nivesh Mitra platform. This scheme is designed to improve connectivity and attract investment to the region.

news.title: Mhada seeks FIR against 23 developers for violating inclusive housing norms, police yet to initiate process
news.para: Maharashtra Housing and Area Development Authority has taken a stand against 23 developers who allegedly defaulted on transferring land designated for affordable housing. This failure reportedly violates inclusive housing laws, raising significant regulatory concerns. While Mhada has called upon the police for intervention, action remains pending, with the next steps hinging on further discussions between Mhada and police officials.
